```{r}
#| include: false
run_targets <- requireNamespace("targets", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("withr", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = run_targets,
  fig.width = 5,
  fig.height = 3.2,
  dpi = 120
)
# size each plot chunk from the plot itself (ggtargets::dag_size()), so
# nodes, lines and text look the same in every figure
knitr::opts_hooks$set(dag_fig = function(options) {
  code <- paste(options$code, collapse = "\n")
  if (!isTRUE(options$eval) || !grepl("ggplot_dag|tar_ggplot", code)) {
    return(options)
  }
  seed <- if (exists(".Random.seed", globalenv())) {
    get(".Random.seed", globalenv())
  }
  wd <- getwd()
  on.exit({
    setwd(wd)
    if (is.null(seed)) {
      suppressWarnings(rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()))
    } else {
      assign(".Random.seed", seed, globalenv())
    }
  })
  root <- knitr::opts_knit$get("root.dir")
  if (!is.null(root)) {
    setwd(root)
  }
  size <- tryCatch(
    {
      p <- eval(parse(text = code), new.env(parent = knitr::knit_global()))
      if (ggplot2::is_ggplot(p) && !inherits(p, "patchwork")) {
        ggtargets::dag_size(p)
      }
    },
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (!is.null(size)) {
    options$fig.width <- size[["width"]]
    options$fig.height <- size[["height"]]
  }
  options
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dag_fig = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(ggtargets)
```

Three example `targets` pipelines, each written with `targets::tar_script()` and plotted in color (the default coloring, or by `type` for the branching one) and by build status, plus a few random graphs at different sizes. The last section collapses two of them: the `analysis` pipeline into its stages, and a random graph into blocks of nodes.

## `basic`: about 6 targets, a straight chain

```{r}
#| label: basic-pipeline
basic_dir <- tempfile("basic")
dir.create(basic_dir)
withr::with_dir(
  basic_dir,
  targets::tar_script({
    tar_option_set(packages = character())

    read_data <- function(n) {
      data.frame(x = seq_len(n), y = seq_len(n) * 2 + stats::rnorm(n))
    }

    clean_data <- function(data) {
      data[stats::complete.cases(data), ]
    }

    fit_model <- function(data) {
      stats::lm(y ~ x, data = data)
    }

    summarize_model <- function(model) {
      data.frame(
        term = names(stats::coef(model)),
        estimate = unname(stats::coef(model))
      )
    }

    write_report <- function(summary) {
      paste(utils::capture.output(print(summary)), collapse = "\n")
    }

    list(
      tar_target(n, 20),
      tar_target(raw_data, read_data(n)),
      tar_target(clean, clean_data(raw_data)),
      tar_target(model, fit_model(clean)),
      tar_target(summary, summarize_model(model)),
      tar_target(report, write_report(summary))
    )
  })
)
```

```{r}
#| label: basic
#| fig-alt: "The basic example pipeline: a short chain of six targets."
withr::with_dir(basic_dir, tar_ggplot())
```

```{r}
#| label: basic-status
#| fig-alt: "The basic pipeline after building it, colored by status (all uptodate)."
withr::with_dir(basic_dir, {
  targets::tar_make(reporter = "silent")
  tar_ggplot(node_color = "status", palette = targets_status_colors())
})
```

## `branching`: dynamic branching over groups

`tar_network()` shows a dynamic branching target's individual branches as one node (with a `branches` count), so the plot has the same size however many branches each target has at runtime. The branched targets have `type = "pattern"`, and are drawn as squares, where the other targets are circles.

```{r}
#| label: branching-pipeline
branching_dir <- tempfile("branching")
dir.create(branching_dir)
withr::with_dir(
  branching_dir,
  targets::tar_script({
    tar_option_set(packages = character())

    make_group_data <- function(group, seed) {
      set.seed(seed)
      data.frame(group = group, value = stats::runif(5))
    }

    clean_group <- function(data, threshold) {
      data[data$value > threshold, ]
    }

    summarize_group <- function(data) {
      data.frame(group = data$group[1], mean = mean(data$value))
    }

    compute_stats <- function(data) {
      data.frame(group = data$group[1], sd = stats::sd(data$value))
    }

    merge_all <- function(summary, stats) {
      merge(summary, stats, by = "group")
    }

    overall_summary <- function(merged) {
      data.frame(
        mean_of_means = mean(merged$mean),
        mean_of_sds = mean(merged$sd)
      )
    }

    write_report <- function(merged, overall) {
      paste(
        utils::capture.output(print(merged)),
        utils::capture.output(print(overall)),
        collapse = "\n"
      )
    }

    list(
      tar_target(seed, 1),
      tar_target(threshold, 0.05),
      tar_target(groups, letters[1:6]),
      tar_target(
        group_data,
        make_group_data(groups, seed),
        pattern = map(groups)
      ),
      tar_target(
        cleaned,
        clean_group(group_data, threshold),
        pattern = map(group_data)
      ),
      tar_target(
        group_summary,
        summarize_group(cleaned),
        pattern = map(cleaned)
      ),
      tar_target(group_stats, compute_stats(cleaned), pattern = map(cleaned)),
      tar_target(merged, merge_all(group_summary, group_stats)),
      tar_target(overall, overall_summary(merged)),
      tar_target(report, write_report(merged, overall))
    )
  })
)
```

```{r}
#| label: branching
#| fig-alt: "The branching example pipeline, targets colored by whether they are a plain target (stem, a circle) or a dynamically branched one (pattern, a square), with one legend for color and shape."
withr::with_dir(branching_dir, tar_ggplot(node_color = "type"))
```

```{r}
#| label: branching-status
#| fig-alt: "The branching pipeline after building it, colored by status."
withr::with_dir(branching_dir, {
  targets::tar_make(reporter = "silent")
  tar_ggplot(node_color = "status", palette = targets_status_colors())
})
```

## `analysis`: about 20 targets, several parallel branches that merge

```{r}
#| label: analysis-pipeline
analysis_dir <- tempfile("analysis")
dir.create(analysis_dir)
withr::with_dir(
  analysis_dir,
  targets::tar_script({
    tar_option_set(packages = character())

    make_config <- function() list(scale = 2, offset = 1)

    load_raw <- function(seed) {
      set.seed(seed)
      stats::rnorm(50)
    }

    clean <- function(x) {
      x[abs(x) < 3]
    }

    feature <- function(x, fn) {
      fn(x)
    }

    combine2 <- function(a, b) {
      c(a, b)
    }

    model_fit <- function(x, config) {
      mean(x) * config$scale + config$offset
    }

    evaluate <- function(model, other = NULL) {
      if (is.null(other)) model else mean(c(model, other))
    }

    report_all <- function(config, ...) {
      vals <- c(...)
      paste(
        "config:",
        config$scale,
        config$offset,
        "| results:",
        paste(round(vals, 3), collapse = ", ")
      )
    }

    # `config` comes first, before any description is set, so it has none
    config_targets <- list(tar_target(config, make_config()))

    tar_option_set(description = "load")
    load_targets <- list(
      tar_target(raw_a, load_raw(1)),
      tar_target(raw_b, load_raw(2)),
      tar_target(raw_c, load_raw(3))
    )

    tar_option_set(description = "clean")
    clean_targets <- list(
      tar_target(clean_a, clean(raw_a)),
      tar_target(clean_b, clean(raw_b)),
      tar_target(clean_c, clean(raw_c))
    )

    tar_option_set(description = "features")
    feature_targets <- list(
      tar_target(feature_a1, feature(clean_a, mean)),
      tar_target(feature_a2, feature(clean_a, stats::median)),
      tar_target(feature_b1, feature(clean_b, mean)),
      tar_target(feature_ab, combine2(feature_a1, feature_b1)),
      tar_target(feature_bc, combine2(clean_b, clean_c))
    )

    tar_option_set(description = "model")
    model_targets <- list(
      tar_target(model_1, model_fit(combine2(feature_a2, feature_ab), config)),
      tar_target(model_2, model_fit(combine2(feature_ab, feature_bc), config)),
      tar_target(model_3, model_fit(combine2(feature_bc, clean_c), config))
    )

    tar_option_set(description = "evaluate")
    eval_targets <- list(
      tar_target(eval_1, evaluate(model_1)),
      tar_target(eval_2, evaluate(model_2, model_1)),
      tar_target(eval_3, evaluate(model_3))
    )

    tar_option_set(description = "report")
    report_targets <- list(
      tar_target(summary_all, combine2(combine2(eval_1, eval_2), eval_3)),
      tar_target(report, report_all(config, summary_all))
    )

    tar_option_set(description = character(0))
    c(
      config_targets,
      load_targets,
      clean_targets,
      feature_targets,
      model_targets,
      eval_targets,
      report_targets
    )
  })
)
```

The targets have a stage in their `description`, set a block at a time with `tar_option_set()`. It doesn't change the plots below, but the [collapsed graphs](#collapsed-graphs) at the end of this page group the targets by it.

```{r}
#| label: analysis
#| fig-alt: "The analysis example pipeline: about 20 targets with several parallel chains that cross and merge, showing crossings and bridges."
withr::with_dir(analysis_dir, tar_ggplot())
```

```{r}
#| label: analysis-status
#| fig-alt: "The analysis pipeline after building it, colored by status."
withr::with_dir(analysis_dir, {
  targets::tar_make(reporter = "silent")
  tar_ggplot(node_color = "status", palette = targets_status_colors())
})
```

## Random graphs at different sizes

```{r}
#| label: random-graph
#| eval: true
random_dag <- function(seed, n, p) {
  set.seed(seed)
  names <- sample(sprintf("n%02d", seq_len(n)))
  from <- to <- character(0)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    for (j in seq_len(n)) {
      if (i < j && runif(1) < p) {
        from <- c(from, sprintf("n%02d", i))
        to <- c(to, sprintf("n%02d", j))
      }
    }
  }
  as_dag(data.frame(from = from, to = to), nodes = data.frame(name = names))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: random-small
#| eval: true
#| fig-alt: "A small random graph with 6 nodes."
ggplot_dag(random_dag(1, 6, 0.3))
```

```{r}
#| label: random-medium
#| eval: true
#| fig-alt: "A medium random graph with 15 nodes and moderate edge density."
ggplot_dag(random_dag(2, 15, 0.15))
```

```{r}
#| label: random-large
#| eval: true
#| fig-alt: "A larger random graph with 30 nodes, showing several crossings and bridges."
ggplot_dag(random_dag(3, 30, 0.08))
```

```{r}
#| label: random-dense
#| eval: true
#| fig-alt: "A densely connected random graph with 20 nodes and high edge probability, showing many crossings."
ggplot_dag(random_dag(4, 20, 0.3))
```

```{r}
#| label: random-sparse
#| eval: true
#| fig-alt: "A sparse random graph with 25 nodes and low edge probability, mostly independent chains."
ggplot_dag(random_dag(5, 25, 0.04))
```

```{r}
#| label: random-custom-style
#| eval: true
#| fig-alt: "A random graph in a custom style: larger nodes, wider arcs."
ggplot_dag(
  random_dag(6, 10, 0.2),
  style = style_metro(node_radius = 8, arc_radius = 18)
)
```

## Collapsed graphs

`tar_ggplot(collapse_by = )` and `dag_collapse()` merge the nodes that share a value of a column into one node, labeled with how many it stands for, and draw one edge for each pair of groups. See the [Collapsing a pipeline](collapsing.html) article for how stages are set and what can go wrong.

### `analysis` by stage

Collapsing the `analysis` pipeline above by its `description` gives one node per stage, with the number of targets in the label. `config`, which has no stage, stays as it is:

```{r}
#| label: analysis-collapsed
#| fig-alt: "The analysis pipeline collapsed to seven nodes, one per row: config, load (3), clean (3), features (5), model (3), evaluate (3) and report (2), joined by lines that bend and cross."
withr::with_dir(analysis_dir, tar_ggplot(collapse_by = "description"))
```

The size of a node and the width of an edge can follow `n`, the number of targets in a node and of dependencies in an edge, and `node_color = "description"` colors the nodes by stage:

```{r}
#| label: analysis-collapsed-sized
#| fig-alt: "The same seven nodes, now of different sizes, the largest for features and the smallest for config, joined by lines of different widths. Each stage has a color, named in a legend, and config, which has no stage, is gray."
withr::with_dir(
  analysis_dir,
  tar_ggplot(
    collapse_by = "description",
    node_color = "description",
    node_size = "n",
    edge_width = "n"
  )
)
```

### A random graph by block

Any DAG can be collapsed by a column of its nodes. Here the 30-node graph from above is grouped in blocks of five consecutive numbers (`n01` to `n05` are block A, and so on). The edges of a random graph run from lower to higher numbers, so the blocks can't make a cycle. `edge_width = "n"` shows how many edges each line stands for:

```{r}
#| label: random-collapsed
#| eval: true
#| fig-alt: "The 30-node random graph collapsed to six nodes, A (5), B (5), C (5), D (5), F (5) and E (5), one per row, joined by lines of different widths."
d <- random_dag(3, 30, 0.08)
d$nodes$block <- LETTERS[(as.integer(substring(d$nodes$name, 2)) - 1) %/% 5 + 1]
ggplot_dag(dag_collapse(d, "block"), edge_width = "n")
```
